$comment: Acceptance rates for agent-authored changes. Recomputed by .github/workflows/acceptance.yml; the interpretation notes are maintained by hand. A raw merged/total ratio would be misleading here, so closures are classified: a PR GitHub auto-closed when its base branch was deleted is not a rejection, and counting it as one would make the number flattering in the wrong direction and useless as a quality signal.
notes: acceptance_rate divides merged by (merged + rejected_on_review). PRs still open and PRs superseded by tooling are excluded from the denominator.

PRs 8 and 9 were auto-closed by GitHub when squash-merging PR 7 deleted their base branch. Both were rebased and reopened as 10 and 11 with identical content. The underlying mistake was stacking PRs on a repo that squash-merges, which does not compose; it was a process error, not a rejected change.
A 100% rate on a solo-maintained repository measures very little on its own. It is recorded so that a later drop is visible, which is the only thing it is good for.
